provenance.name: data provenance
provenance.definition: A record of where data came from, what terms govern it, and which transformations produced a derived corpus artifact.
provenance.explanation: Useful provenance connects each retained document to a source, author or publisher when known, license or terms, retrieval context, identity, and processing recipe. It supports reproducibility, rights review, debugging, and removal requests. A URL or mirror license does not establish rights to the text itself. Provenance records evidence rather than guaranteeing legality or quality. Later model checkpoints should refer to the exact corpus manifest and tokenizer so results can be traced to their inputs.

near-duplicate.name: near duplicate
near-duplicate.definition: A document substantially overlapping another after small formatting or content changes.
near-duplicate.explanation: Exact hashes miss copies that add navigation, alter whitespace, or edit a few words. Near-duplicate detectors compare features such as token shingles and remove pairs above a recorded threshold. The choice balances repeated-content leakage against false removal of legitimately related documents. Deduplication order also decides which copy survives. At scale, approximate search reduces cost, while an exact small implementation can remain an oracle. Removed-to-retained links make the decision auditable.

contamination.name: evaluation contamination
contamination.definition: Training exposure to evaluation items, answers, or close variants that weakens the meaning of held-out scores.
contamination.explanation: Contamination can arise through exact document copies, quoted benchmark questions, solution pages, neighboring windows, or semantic variants. This chapter's whole-document comparison removes exact and detected near duplicates before split assignment. It does not find embedded passages or paraphrases, and its split artifact cannot force a downstream window builder to respect document boundaries. Every detector has false negatives and false positives, so a clean report is evidence under a stated method rather than proof of absence.
